sentences.text: Let's start a long way back, and a little to the west.
This block is a schematic, not to scale: the ancient Highlands gneiss that lies beneath and beyond the edge of the basin, more than a billion years old.
Inside it sit deposits of magnetite, rich in uranium, thorium and rare earth elements.

This block is a schematic, not to scale: the ancient Highlands gneiss that lies beneath and beyond the edge of the basin, more than a billion years old. Inside it sit deposits of magnetite, rich in uranium, thorium and rare earth elements.

sentences.text: Nearby are younger Neoproterozoic ironstones, carrying hematite, uranium, thorium and tungsten.
Together with the gneiss and the magnetite, these are the only rocks in New Jersey rich enough in those elements to be the source of what we later find in the carnelian.

sentences.text: Around two hundred million years ago the crust stretched and broke.
The Newark basin dropped down along its border fault and filled with red sediment, and lava flows, the Preakness among them, spread across it.

beats.text: Around two hundred million years ago the crust stretched and broke. The Newark basin dropped down along its border fault and filled with red sediment, and lava flows, the Preakness among them, spread across it.

sentences.text: Rain water sank along the border fault, deep into the hot basement.
Fluid inclusions and reset fission tracks tell us it reached somewhere between one hundred and two hundred and eighty degrees Celsius, turned acidic, and picked up chlorine and fluorine.
Water like that strips uranium, thorium, niobium, tungsten and rare earths out of the rock.

beats.text: Rain water sank along the border fault, deep into the hot basement. Fluid inclusions and reset fission tracks tell us it reached somewhere between one hundred and two hundred and eighty degrees Celsius, turned acidic, and picked up chlorine and fluorine. Water like that strips uranium, thorium, niobium, tungsten and rare earths out of the rock.

sentences.text: Heated and loaded with those elements, the fluid rose again along faults inside the basin, toward the young Preakness lava.
Nearly every trace element later measured in the carnelian can be traced to this journey.

beats.text: Heated and loaded with those elements, the fluid rose again along faults inside the basin, toward the young Preakness lava. Nearly every trace element later measured in the carnelian can be traced to this journey.

sentences.text: Now we move to the basin floor itself, a little over two hundred and one million years ago.
This is a six by five kilometre block around the Green Brook site, with the beds laid flat, as they were deposited.
The faint ghost above is today's land surface, just for orientation.
The floor is the Orange Mountain Basalt: more than two hundred metres of older lava, already in place.

This is a six by five kilometre block around the Green Brook site, with the beds laid flat, as they were deposited. The faint ghost above is today's land surface, just for orientation. The floor is the Orange Mountain Basalt: more than two hundred metres of older lava, already in place.

sentences.text: Rivers begin to spread reddish-brown sand and silt across the floodplain.
This is the Feltville Formation.

beats.text: Rivers begin to spread reddish-brown sand and silt across the floodplain. This is the Feltville Formation.

sentences.text: Early on, a lake forms.
It leaves three metres of black carbonaceous shale, limestone and calcareous siltstone.

beats.text: Early on, a lake forms. It leaves three metres of black carbonaceous shale, limestone and calcareous siltstone.

sentences.text: A second lake sequence follows about fifteen metres higher.
Both carry fossils of fish, reptiles and plants.

beats.text: A second lake sequence follows about fifteen metres higher. Both carry fossils of fish, reptiles and plants.

sentences.text: Then the red river beds just keep coming, until the Feltville is a hundred and forty-five metres thick.
That thickness is measured.
How long it took is not something the sources tell us.

beats.text: Then the red river beds just keep coming, until the Feltville is a hundred and forty-five metres thick. That thickness is measured. How long it took is not something the sources tell us.

sentences.text: And here is the top of the Feltville.
The first Preakness flow will land on this surface and bake its upper half metre.

beats.text: And here is the top of the Feltville. The first Preakness flow will land on this surface and bake its upper half metre.

sentences.text: Two hundred and one million years ago.
The Feltville floodplain lies partly under shallow water, and our cut face runs from north-west to south-east through the Green Brook site.

beats.text: Two hundred and one million years ago. The Feltville floodplain lies partly under shallow water, and our cut face runs from north-west to south-east through the Green Brook site.

sentences.text: Lava arrives and meets standing water.
Where it chills it forms a glass rind only a couple of centimetres thick, and pillow lobes, each about the size of a beach ball, pile up through the lowest few metres of the flow.

beats.text: Lava arrives and meets standing water. Where it chills it forms a glass rind only a couple of centimetres thick, and pillow lobes, each about the size of a beach ball, pile up through the lowest few metres of the flow.

sentences.text: Above the pillows, the lower flow cools into the colonnade: slender columns no more than half a metre wide and six metres long.

beats.text: Above the pillows, the lower flow cools into the colonnade: slender columns no more than half a metre wide and six metres long.

sentences.text: The flow is thick, and its interior stays molten for a long time.
Crystals settle and sort, and build a coarse-grained lens called gabbroid: eighty-two metres thick here, forty-nine at Stirling Brook.
It is the thickest gabbroid in the basin, and it is the reason carnelian turns up here and nowhere else.

beats.text: The flow is thick, and its interior stays molten for a long time. Crystals settle and sort, and build a coarse-grained lens called gabbroid: eighty-two metres thick here, forty-nine at Stirling Brook. It is the thickest gabbroid in the basin, and it is the reason carnelian turns up here and nowhere else.

sentences.text: Gas rising through the flow is trapped beneath that coarse barrier.
It collects in six thin vesicle-rich sheets in the upper forty metres, with up to nineteen percent bubbles, around a band rich in black glass.
Keep an eye on these sheets.
This is where the carnelian will grow.

beats.text: Gas rising through the flow is trapped beneath that coarse barrier. It collects in six thin vesicle-rich sheets in the upper forty metres, with up to nineteen percent bubbles, around a band rich in black glass. Keep an eye on these sheets. This is where the carnelian will grow.

sentences.text: The top of the flow freezes as a crust two and a half metres thick and full of bubbles: the amygdaloidal flow top.
The paper names it as the other candidate for the carnelian's birthplace.

beats.text: The top of the flow freezes as a crust two and a half metres thick and full of bubbles: the amygdaloidal flow top. The paper names it as the other candidate for the carnelian's birthplace.

sentences.text: And then it is done.
A hundred and forty-five metres of basalt, cooled, with a gabbroid lens in its upper half.

beats.text: And then it is done. A hundred and forty-five metres of basalt, cooled, with a gabbroid lens in its upper half.

sentences.text: This is the heart of the story.
Hot, acidic fluid, shown as the red particles, rises from depth along the columns and faults into the upper part of the first flow.

beats.text: This is the heart of the story. Hot, acidic fluid, shown as the red particles, rises from depth along the columns and faults into the upper part of the first flow.

sentences.text: From above, cool, more alkaline rain water sinks to meet it: the blue particles.
Where they mix, the temperature settles mostly between twenty and eighty degrees, and the water turns neutral to slightly alkaline.
That mixing zone is the coloured field.

beats.text: From above, cool, more alkaline rain water sinks to meet it: the blue particles. Where they mix, the temperature settles mostly between twenty and eighty degrees, and the water turns neutral to slightly alkaline. That mixing zone is the coloured field.

sentences.text: Glass in the gabbroid breaks down and releases silica into the mix.
Now, where exactly did the carnelian form?
The paper offers two candidates and does not choose between them: zone A, the six vesicle-rich sheets, and zone B, the bubbly flow top.

beats.text: Glass in the gabbroid breaks down and releases silica into the mix. Now, where exactly did the carnelian form? The paper offers two candidates and does not choose between them: zone A, the six vesicle-rich sheets, and zone B, the bubbly flow top.

sentences.text: Let's go inside.
This is one gas bubble, eight millimetres across, in the uppermost sheet; the view is about a centimetre and a half wide.
A crystal of glauberite, a sodium calcium sulphate, is already sitting in it.

beats.text: Let's go inside. This is one gas bubble, eight millimetres across, in the uppermost sheet; the view is about a centimetre and a half wide. A crystal of glauberite, a sodium calcium sulphate, is already sitting in it.

sentences.text: Silica begins to come out of solution.
Fibres of chalcedony nucleate on the bumpy floor of the bubble and grow upward.

beats.text: Silica begins to come out of solution. Fibres of chalcedony nucleate on the bumpy floor of the bubble and grow upward.

sentences.text: As the fill thickens, its top takes the grape-like, botryoidal shape seen on the real pieces.
Tiny inclusions of hematite give it the red colour.
This is carnelian.

beats.text: As the fill thickens, its top takes the grape-like, botryoidal shape seen on the real pieces. Tiny inclusions of hematite give it the red colour. This is carnelian.

sentences.text: Later, the glauberite dissolves and leaves a mold.
It is this order of events, bubble, then glauberite, then carnelian, that the paper reads from the textures.

beats.text: Later, the glauberite dissolves and leaves a mold. It is this order of events, bubble, then glauberite, then carnelian, that the paper reads from the textures.

sentences.text: Under the microscope, at two thousand times, the carnelian shows bundles of length-fast fibres rising from the attachment band, crossed by rhythmic extinction bands.
This is the texture that confirmed the growth sequence.

beats.text: Under the microscope, at two thousand times, the carnelian shows bundles of length-fast fibres rising from the attachment band, crossed by rhythmic extinction bands. This is the texture that confirmed the growth sequence.

sentences.text: The first flow now lies open to the sky.
Its bubbly top weathers and erodes.
For how long, we do not know.

beats.text: The first flow now lies open to the sky. Its bubbly top weathers and erodes. For how long, we do not know.

sentences.text: A river lays two to three metres of reddish siltstone and shale on it.
That thin layer is proof that the flow top was once a land surface.

beats.text: A river lays two to three metres of reddish siltstone and shale on it. That thin layer is proof that the flow top was once a land surface.

sentences.text: Then the second Preakness flow erupts over it: massive basalt, with pipe vesicles at its base, about seventy metres thick.

beats.text: Then the second Preakness flow erupts over it: massive basalt, with pipe vesicles at its base, about seventy metres thick.

sentences.text: More flows follow, until the Preakness is three hundred and fifteen metres thick in total.

beats.text: More flows follow, until the Preakness is three hundred and fifteen metres thick in total.

sentences.text: Then the Towaco Formation, nearly four hundred metres of red beds, buries everything.
The carnelian horizon is now several hundred metres down.

beats.text: Then the Towaco Formation, nearly four hundred metres of red beds, buries everything. The carnelian horizon is now several hundred metres down.

sentences.text: Deep burial warms the rocks.
Hydrocarbons in the Feltville show that it reached ninety to a hundred and thirty degrees, a ceiling the paper uses when it tests the fluid temperatures.

beats.text: Deep burial warms the rocks. Hydrocarbons in the Feltville show that it reached ninety to a hundred and thirty degrees, a ceiling the paper uses when it tests the fluid temperatures.

sentences.text: Time to tilt.
As the Watchung syncline folds, the whole stack rotates about nine and a half degrees toward the north-west.
The attitude comes from the Chatham map's cross-section.
When it happened, the paper does not say.

beats.text: Time to tilt. As the Watchung syncline folds, the whole stack rotates about nine and a half degrees toward the north-west. The attitude comes from the Chatham map's cross-section. When it happened, the paper does not say.

sentences.text: Uplift follows.
By the middle to late Miocene a broad river plain lies at or above the highest basalt summits, more than fifty metres above where the carnelian sites are today.

beats.text: Uplift follows. By the middle to late Miocene a broad river plain lies at or above the highest basalt summits, more than fifty metres above where the carnelian sites are today.

sentences.text: Then, through the Pliocene and Pleistocene, the rivers cut down.
The deep valley on the soft Feltville red beds, between the two basalt ridges, forms first.

beats.text: Then, through the Pliocene and Pleistocene, the rivers cut down. The deep valley on the soft Feltville red beds, between the two basalt ridges, forms first.

sentences.text: Only later do headwater tributaries, Green Brook and Stirling Brook, bite back into the Preakness ridge.
Their valley sides reach the carnelian horizon: the six sheets, outlined here.

beats.text: Only later do headwater tributaries, Green Brook and Stirling Brook, bite back into the Preakness ridge. Their valley sides reach the carnelian horizon: the six sheets, outlined here.

sentences.text: Where the horizon meets the surface, marked by the red dots, pieces of carnelian weather out, then creep and wash down the slope into Green Brook.
The pieces are drawn three metres across so that you can see them at this scale.

beats.text: Where the horizon meets the surface, marked by the red dots, pieces of carnelian weather out, then creep and wash down the slope into Green Brook. The pieces are drawn three metres across so that you can see them at this scale.

sentences.text: And this is today's surface, from the lidar.
The carnelian horizon still runs through the valley sides, hidden under soil and rock debris.

beats.text: And this is today's surface, from the lidar. The carnelian horizon still runs through the valley sides, hidden under soil and rock debris.

sentences.text: Ice came close, twice.
In the early Pleistocene a glacier stopped at the dashed line marked M one.
Its till survives in the headwaters of Green Brook's north-eastern tributary.
Stirling Brook lies two kilometres south of that line.

beats.text: Ice came close, twice. In the early Pleistocene a glacier stopped at the dashed line marked M one. Its till survives in the headwaters of Green Brook's north-eastern tributary. Stirling Brook lies two kilometres south of that line.

sentences.text: Much later, the late Wisconsinan ice sheet built its terminal moraine and dammed glacial Lake Passaic, at the line marked M two, well to the north.
Neither glacier reached the carnelian brooks.

beats.text: Much later, the late Wisconsinan ice sheet built its terminal moraine and dammed glacial Lake Passaic, at the line marked M two, well to the north. Neither glacier reached the carnelian brooks.

sentences.text: Today, at Green Brook, the cut face shows the cover: colluvium up to eighteen metres thick and alluvium up to three, resting on the bedrock top.
The trace of the carnelian horizon runs along the valley sides beneath it.

beats.text: Today, at Green Brook, the cut face shows the cover: colluvium up to eighteen metres thick and alluvium up to three, resting on the bedrock top. The trace of the carnelian horizon runs along the valley sides beneath it.

sentences.text: Down at the brook, a gravel bar of basalt and gabbroid cobbles rests on a pavement of gabbroid.
Among the cobbles are the carnelian pebbles, one to five and a half centimetres across, drawn larger here.

beats.text: Down at the brook, a gravel bar of basalt and gabbroid cobbles rests on a pavement of gabbroid. Among the cobbles are the carnelian pebbles, one to five and a half centimetres across, drawn larger here.

sentences.text: A flood rises, and muddy water covers the bar.

beats.text: A flood rises, and muddy water covers the bar.

sentences.text: At peak flow the current scours the alluvium off the bed and exposes the hidden bedrock source, the outline you see here.
This is the paper's second scenario.

beats.text: At peak flow the current scours the alluvium off the bed and exposes the hidden bedrock source, the outline you see here. This is the paper's second scenario.

sentences.text: As the water drops, fresh pebbles are left in the bar, or not.
Under the first scenario the source is largely gone and the supply thins with every flood.
Under the second, floods keep delivering.
You can switch between them in the panel at the left.

sentences.text: After the flood.
The paper prefers replenishment: collectors have kept finding carnelian here for decades.

sentences.text: Finally, let's follow one piece.
Two hundred and one million years ago, inside a bubble eight millimetres across in the upper first flow, silica from the mixing fluids builds a nodule, fibre by fibre, beside a glauberite crystal.

sentences.text: The second flow, the rest of the Preakness and the Towaco red beds pile on top.
The nodule sits several hundred metres down, at ninety to a hundred and thirty degrees.

sentences.text: The Watchung syncline folds, and the rock around the nodule tilts nine and a half degrees to the north-west.

sentences.text: Erosion cuts the Green Brook valley down to the horizon.
Frost, roots and water loosen the vesicular rock, and the nodule falls free at the real outcrop of the sheets, on the real hillside.

The cut wall beside the path shows the modelled layers underneath.
